Days to close a punch item per month

Open Start and type your studio name and your own limits in the yellow cells: grace days for a late delivery, free storage days, the notice a trade needs, the cost of a day of delay and the punch fixes a fixer closes in a day.
Check Team, Vendors, Contractors and Projects. They hold the people, vendors, trades and projects that every other sheet looks up.
Log every delivery on Deliveries with the promised and scheduled dates. Days late, the due-in-seven-days flag and the late check fill in; Delivery Weeks counts them week by week.
On the day a delivery arrives add a row on Receiving Checks. Damage or a missing item goes to Damage Claims, and a replacement to Replacement Orders with its promised date.
Keep Items by Room up to date with delivered and installed dates. Room Readiness shows which rooms are ready for the crew and which are waiting.
Plan every installation day on Installation Schedule and every trade booking on Trade Calendar. Site Access holds the hours, parking, lift and keys of each project.
Record each trade job on Trade Jobs with its quote. The overrun and the average overrun by contractor fill in when you enter the actual cost.
Write each finishing fix on Punch List. Punch by Project shows the close-out share and the oldest open item; Handover Items holds what is left at the walk-through.
Track Warehouse Storage for lots held at the receiving warehouse and Project Photos for the shoots after each handover.

Use the 14 calculators for installation order, delivery slots, receiving counts, damage claims, room ready dates, trade overruns, storage, punch forecasts, crew days, handover dates, delay costs and what-ifs.
Read the Installation Dashboard and Charts every week: late deliveries, damage, rooms ready, trade overruns, punch items and handovers.

Time entries with value, cost and week
One row per block of time a team member logs on a project and phase; the billable value, the labour cost at the hour cost and the week fill in by themselves.
Timesheet by week with utilisation and value
One row per team member and week: hours and billable hours; the utilisation against the weekly capacity, the billable share and the billing value fill in by themselves.
Time value by project and month, billed or not
One row per hourly project and month: billable hours, their value and the invoice; the unbilled value, the days after month-end and the credit applied fill in by themselves.
Client invoices with days late, state and open amount
One row per client invoice: kind, amount, dates and status; the days outstanding, days late, state, open and overdue amounts fill in by themselves.
Invoices still to come or open, by due date
One row per invoice that is planned, sent or overdue: kind, amount, planned invoice date, due date and trigger; the days to the due date, the week and the state fill in by themselves.
Retainers paid, credited and still held
One row per retainer invoice: amount, dates and the amount credited against fee invoices; the credit left, days to pay and the check fill in by themselves.
Fee milestones with share, due date and billing
One row per fee milestone of a fixed-fee project: share, amount, due date and the invoice; the project fee, billing check and days to the due date fill in by themselves.
FF&E deposit and balance invoices against the ordered value
One row per FF&E invoice: deposit or balance, amount, ordered value and status; the share of the ordered value, the billed share of the project and the due date fill in by themselves.
One row per contractor invoice re-billed to the client: contractor cost, mark-up and billed amount; the margin, the mark-up really applied and a mark-up check fill in by themselves.
Payments received with month and days after the due date
One row per payment received: invoice, date, amount, method and bank reference; the client, the month and the days after the due date fill in by themselves.
Clients with invoiced, paid, open balance and lateness
One row per client or prospect: kind, contact, payment terms and stage; the invoiced and paid totals, the open balance, the average days late and a payer check fill in by themselves.
Projects with fee type, billed, paid and balance
One row per project: client, fee type, fee, hours and values; the billed and paid totals from the invoices, the balance, the fee billed and the fixed fee over hours check fill in by themselves.
Project profit and margin per hour, completed first
One row per project: hours and labour cost at the hour cost; the fee billed, FF&E and trades margins, the margin after labour, the margin per hour and the fee per hour fill in for completed projects.
Chase steps for late invoices with promises kept or broken
One row per reminder, call or notice sent for a late invoice: step, channel, promise date and outcome; the days overdue, the amount and whether the promise was kept fill in by themselves.
Reminder rules by client kind and step
One row per client kind and reminder step: days after the due date, channel, tone and who sends; the sender phone fills in from the team.
Credit notes and write-offs with running total
One row per credit note or write-off: invoice, date, amount, reason and who approved it; the client, the share of the invoice and the running total fill in by themselves.
Statement of account per client, overdue first
One row per client with invoices: the last statement date; the totals, the overdue amount, the oldest open invoice and the call priority fill in by themselves.
Billing rates with cost and margin per hour
One row per service hour the studio bills: role, billing rate and hour cost; the margin per hour, the rate over cost and a margin check fill in by themselves.
Projects whose hours cost more than the fee
One row per fixed-fee or percentage-fee project: the extra fee recovered; the fee, hours at hour cost, amount over the fee and the checks fill in by themselves.
Team with hour cost, bill rate and the last four weeks
The owner designer, four staff and seven freelance specialists: role, hours a week, hour cost and bill rate; the margin per hour and the hours logged in the last four weeks fill in by themselves.
